title: I'm Running Ten Minutes Late
observable_outcome: The learner writes a short delay message that states the problem, gives an expected arrival time, and promises an update if needed.
learning_objective: Report a delay, give an expected arrival time, and promise an update if the time changes.

scenario.prompt: Your shift starts at 8:00 a.m. It is 7:48. Your bus is diverted. The journey screen now shows 22 minutes. You expect to arrive at 8:10.
scenario.puzzle: What should you tell your manager now? Which details help them plan?
scenario.privacy_note: The workplace, route, names, times, and messages are fictional teaching data. This activity is language practice, not employment advice.

model.opening: Hi Sam, I'm sorry, but my bus has been diverted.
model.delay: I'm running about ten minutes late.
model.update: I'll message you if that changes.
model.full_message: Hi Sam, I'm sorry, but my bus has been diverted. I'm running about ten minutes late. I expect to arrive at 8:10. I'll message you if that changes.
neutral_variants: I'm delayed and expect to arrive at about 8:10.
My bus is delayed. I should arrive around 8:10.

language_focus.grammar: I'm running late uses am plus the -ing form. Here it describes a situation developing now. I expect to arrive uses the present simple to state your current estimate. I'll message uses will for a decision or promise made now.
language_focus.meaning: About ten minutes late describes the delay. At 8:10 gives the expected arrival time. These are related, but they are not the same detail.
language_focus.appropriateness: Contact the relevant person early. State the delay and expected arrival plainly. A brief apology can acknowledge the impact. Avoid excuses you cannot verify. Follow the real workplace process.
language_focus.pronunciation: In speech, stress ten minutes and 8:10. I'm contracts I am. I'll contracts I will. The details carry the message, so say them clearly.
language_focus.workplace_note: Workplace notification rules differ. Use the required channel, and update your estimate if it changes.

evidence_activity.prompt: Which message helps the manager plan?

options.text: I'm sorry. My bus has been diverted. I expect to arrive at 8:10.
options.feedback: Correct. It states the cause and gives a usable arrival time.

options.text: Something happened. I'll be there later.
options.feedback: This gives no expected arrival time. The manager still cannot plan.

options.text: The bus system is terrible today.
options.feedback: This expresses frustration. It does not state your delay or arrival time.

question_activity.prompt: It is 7:48. The journey takes 22 minutes. Which arrival estimate matches the evidence?

options.feedback: The new journey time passes the 8:00 start. Do not promise the original time.
This is too broad. The journey screen supports a closer estimate.

slot_activity.prompt: Match each message part to its job.

feedback.cause: Correct. This names the current problem.
feedback.delay: The delay is about ten minutes.

feedback.cause: The cause is the bus diversion.
The cause is the bus diversion.
feedback.delay: The delay is about ten minutes.
feedback.arrival: Correct. This gives the expected clock time.

feedback.cause: The cause is the bus diversion.
feedback.delay: The delay is about ten minutes.
feedback.follow-up: Correct. This promises a later update.

production_task.scenario: A training session starts at 2:00 p.m. It is 1:50. Your delayed bus now shows 22 minutes. You expect to arrive at 2:12.
production_task.instruction: Write one short message. Apologize briefly, state the delay, give the expected arrival time, and promise an update if needed.
acceptable_responses: Hi Maya, I'm sorry, but my bus is delayed. I'm running about twelve minutes late and expect to arrive at 2:12. I'll message you if that changes.
Sorry, my bus has been delayed. I should arrive around 2:12. I'll update you if the time changes.
production_task.valid_variants: Expect to arrive, should arrive, and think I'll arrive can all give an estimate. About and around show that the time is not guaranteed. A short message may omit the cause when privacy or uncertainty matters, but it should still give the delay and expected arrival.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, recall the four message parts: cause, delay, arrival, and follow-up.

design.texture: Restrained fibres and speckles generated procedurally.
design.depth: Vehicles, people, clocks, signs, and message tiles use cream cut edges, overlaps, and offset shadows.
design.motion_principle: The bus travels, meets a detour, changes route, and reaches a later clock. Message tiles enter in sequence while clock hands pivot. Motion demonstrates the changing arrival estimate.
design.accessibility: Dark navy text sits on cream panels. Every colour relationship also has words, numbers, arrows, and shape labels.

visual.title: Notice, calculate, message
visual.alt_text: A colourful layered papercut path. A bus diverted at 7:48 follows a detour. A 22-minute journey strip leads to an 8:10 arrival clock. Four message cards name the cause, delay, arrival, and follow-up.
visual.prose: First notice the changed journey time. Calculate the expected arrival. Then write four message parts: cause, delay, arrival, and follow-up. The arrival time helps the other person plan.
